prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” — the right company depends on your priorities (price, speed, attention to detail, eco‑friendly paints, warranty, etc.). I can’t browse current local listings from here, but I can help you find the best interior painter in St. Louis by giving a reliable process, what to look for, and sample questions to ask.

How to find top local painters
- Search local review sites: Google Maps, Yelp, Angi (HomeAdvisor), BBB, Nextdoor, and local Facebook groups.  
- Ask neighbors or recent remodelers for referrals and to see work in person.  
- Shortlist 3–5 companies with strong recent reviews and good photo portfolios.

What to check before hiring
- License/registration (if applicable in MO) and proof of liability insurance and workers’ comp.  
- References from recent jobs and photos of completed interiors similar to yours.  
- Written estimate/contract with scope, materials, brand/finish of paint, number of coats, prep work, timeline, payment schedule, cleanup, and warranty/guarantee.  
- Experience with any special needs (high ceilings, trim/detail work, faux finishes, low‑VOC paints).

Important questions to ask each painter
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see certificates?  
- Do you provide a written estimate and written contract? What is included?  
- Which paint brands and finishes do you use? Are low‑VOC options available?  
- How many coats will you apply to walls/trim/ceiling? Is primer included?  
- How will you protect floors/furniture and handle touchups?  
- What is your projected start date and completion time?  
- Do you offer a warranty or guarantee on workmanship? How long?

What a clear written estimate should include
- Labor and materials separated.  
- Prep details (patching, sanding, caulking, priming).  
- Paint brand, color names/codes, number of coats.  
- Items included/excluded (doors, closets, trim, ceilings).  
- Start/completion dates, payment schedule, cleanup, and warranty.

Typical cost ballpark (interior painting, US, varies by project)
- Per room: roughly $300–$800 for a standard bedroom; larger rooms or rooms with heavy prep cost more.  
- Per square foot: commonly $1.50–$4.00 per sq ft (includes labor + materials) depending on prep, ceilings/trim, and paint quality.  
These are rough estimates; get multiple written quotes.

Red flags
- No written contract or insurance proof.  
- Very low bid with no itemized scope.  
- Poor communication, missed appointments, or pressure for large deposit (standard is smaller deposit with balance on completion).

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short RFP/message you can send to painters.  
- Provide a checklist to compare written estimates side‑by‑side.  
- Review estimates or company profiles if you paste them here.  
- Suggest likely local companies if you give a St. Louis ZIP code (I can’t browse, but I can suggest typical franchised names you might look up).

Tell me: what room(s) are you painting, your ZIP code, and any priorities (budget, eco‑friendly paints, timeline), and I’ll help you choose next steps or draft messages to painters.
